rows.title: The INS front door's home becomes the overall dashboard, with the performance suite's checks following its heading
rows.detail: Today the INS front door's root page is a table of every notification with a reference search and a sort form. It becomes the service's home: a 'Dashboard' caption over the heading 'Import notification service', the 'Create new' and 'Use template' buttons, then one section per notification category, each linking to that category's own notification list in its own frontend. The home's controls are built on today's home before this and stay when it lands. The k6 performance suite checks the home's heading and models its reads, so it changes in the same increment as the heading, never before: changing the suite first breaks every performance run, and changing the heading first makes the suite's readiness check fail after 300 seconds. The home's per-category summary waits until the notification dashboard's requirements are firmed up and agreed.
acceptanceCriteria: A signed-in trader opening the INS front door's home sees a page whose main content is, in order, the caption, the heading, the 'Create new' and 'Use template' buttons and one section per notification category (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11539-11545; trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 8-9; trace:ins-fit trace-ins-fit-p4-005; conflicts:c-145)

The home shows the caption 'Dashboard' directly above the h1 'Import notification service', while its browser title stays 'Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:23-24; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:14-16; conflicts:c-146)
'Create new' and 'Use template' show under the heading (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:34-42; conflicts:c-147)

Below them the home shows a 'Live animals' section then a 'Plants, plant products or other objects' section, each with an h2 heading and a 'View dashboard' link (trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 27-31; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:34-38)

Following the Live animals section's 'View dashboard' shows the live animals notification list at the live-animals set root in the animals frontend (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:46-53; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p15-115; conflicts:c-250, c-295)

The plants section's heading reads 'Plants, plant products or' with a line break before 'other objects', in the section's plants style, and following its 'View dashboard' shows the high-risk plants dashboard at the high-risk-plants set base on the plants frontend (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:100-131; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p15-117; conflicts:c-151)

When the notification read model cannot be loaded, the home still shows its caption and heading, shows the service's recoverable error message, responds with HTTP status 500 and logs the failure; an error already shaped for the framework is passed on unchanged (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-058)

With Welsh selected, the home's caption, heading, section headings, section links and glance-card copy show in Welsh, as do the Action needed, Status updated and Inspection required pages, every Welsh string marked as a machine draft that does not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-086)
The home has no serious or critical axe violations against the WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA tags (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-079)

The k6 performance suite's check of the INS home requests '/' under the endpoint name 'ins-dashboard' and passes when the home answers 200 with the main heading 'Import notification service' (repo:perftests repo-perftests-p2-001, repo-perftests-p2-003; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-004; conflicts:c-146)

The k6 suite models the INS home's load on the read model as the per-category count reads the home makes, and its check of how many notifications the read model holds reads that count from the read model (repo:perftests repo-perftests-p2-015, repo-perftests-p2-044; repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-062)

The 'INS signed-in page' readiness probe passes when the INS home answers 200 to a signed-in trader with the main heading 'Import notification service' (repo:perftests repo-perftests-p2-040; conflicts:c-146)
The 'address book read' readiness probe passes when the INS address book answers 200 with the heading 'Address book' (repo:perftests repo-perftests-p2-041)
The stack counts as ready only when one pass succeeds for all six probes; otherwise readiness fails after 300 seconds, naming the probes that failed (repo:perftests repo-perftests-p2-042)
rows.gate: Once unblocked and built, look at the new home on a local stack before the glance cards and drill-downs are built on it: the caption and heading, the buttons kept under it, the category sections and where their View dashboard links land, and that the rewritten INS end-to-end specs no longer depend on the removed table.
openQuestions: Blocked: Sam's 9 October rulings block the INS dashboard's summary information (the overall home's per-category sections, counts and glance cards, the status-change cards and their drill-downs) until its requirements firm up and are agreed; the area is then re-distilled. Who: whoever owns the INS dashboard's requirements (the rulings do not name them) must firm them up and agree them with Sam.

Blocked: req-1905's readiness probe and req-1848's k6 home check change only with the home's heading (c-146); changing them first breaks every performance run on main, so they wait with the rest of the overall home and keep 'Dashboard' until it lands. Who: the same owner of the INS dashboard's requirements.
notes: Combines the home shell, the category sections and their links, and the home's error, Welsh, accessibility and performance-suite requirements: all are the same page and the same set-up, so building them apart would repeat the same review and ladder. req-971's three-section order completes when the Germinal products section row lands.

req-1905 (the performance suite's readiness probe expecting the new h1) belongs to the layout-and-sign-in area, not this one, but has sat in this row since the last distil and must stay with req-1848 so the suite is never broken on main. The combiner should keep it here and not let the layout-and-sign-in draft take it into a second row.

Rewritten against the wording rules, keeping the row's id: the old title and detail named the design release, the old detail carried conflict ids, and the first criterion quoted the removed 'Search by notification reference' field and 'Showing x-y of z' label. The first criterion is now an exhaustive positive check on what the home's main content holds, which proves the table's removal without naming it.

The home changes the INS dashboard feature's controller, template, copy and fit spec, and the tests repo's INS dashboard page object, which the split-off type-question-and-templates theme owns, and the dashboard view-model, which the split-off overview-and-review theme owns. These requirements were already in this row, in the ins-dashboard theme, when those themes split off, so they are not a later adoption to hand to a pickUp list. The row builds only after type-question-and-templates lands (externalDependsOn inc-149 and inc-153, and ins-dashboard depends on that theme), so its changes to those files never conflict. They are therefore listed in shared, not touches.

For the combiner: the k6 check of the INS home's heading sits in two places, perftests src/k6/front-door.js:58 as well as src/k6/readiness.js:39 (both confirmed on main). front-door.js is in the split-off address-book theme's touches, so that half of req-1848 overlaps a split-off theme's code; it was in this row before that split, so it stays here, and it is listed in shared.

Removing the table breaks the tests repo's INS dashboard page object (it finds the page by the h1 'Dashboard' and the reference search) and notification-dashboard-navigation.spec.ts; both are rewritten in this row, after the split-off theme lands.

rows.title: The Action needed page lists the organisation's notifications needing action
rows.detail: Each category's Action needed glance card opens a page listing the notifications the trader must act on: a submitted notification still missing a required document, or with no animal identifier where one is required, which the animals backend records as its 'Submitted action required' status. The INS front door lists those notifications, across every category or only the one it is showing, scoped to the signed-in organisation, with an intro block, a results line, eight notifications a page and the same notification card the category list uses. It waits until the notification dashboard's requirements are firmed up and agreed; how the action-required state and the category reach the INS read model is settled then.
acceptanceCriteria: The 'View tasks' link opens a page at /actions whose browser title is 'Tasks requiring your attention - Import notification service - GOV.UK', showing the caption 'Action needed', the h1 'Tasks requiring your attention' and the description 'Add missing information or upload documents to prevent your consignment from being delayed.', the three together as one intro block styled to match the home's intro rather than as a plain caption-above-heading pair (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11708-11710, app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-actions.html:34-36; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:153-159; conflicts:c-156)

A live-animals notification submitted without its ITAHC or health certificate is listed with an 'Action required' status tag and the message 'ITAHC is missing'; once the certificate is uploaded and the notification re-submitted, the page lists it no longer (trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed action 14-16; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p15-087; conflicts:c-149)

A submitted notification with its certificate but a species that needs identifiers and none identified is listed with the message 'Information is missing'; once one identifier is filled for each record, the page lists it no longer (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-149; conflicts:c-149)

The page lists only submitted notifications missing a required document or a required animal identifier, one identifier being enough for a record to count as identified: a draft notification, and a submitted one with every required document and identifier, are absent from it (trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed snapshot 14; conflicts:c-149)

A trader signed in for one organisation sees only that organisation's notifications on the page, and a fresh organisation with none sees 'Show 0 of 0 results' (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-068; trace:ins-fit trace-ins-fit-p4-046)

Opened with no category, the page lists action-needed notifications of every category; opened for live animals it lists only live-animals ones, a notification with no stored category counting as live animals; an unrecognised category lists every category (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:6745-6747, 9027-9028; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:162-169; conflicts:c-296)

The page's 'Back' link goes to the live animals notification list at the live-animals set root in the animals frontend while it is showing live animals, and to the home while it is showing every category or an unrecognised one (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-actions.html:12-24; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:156, 167; conflicts:c-250, c-295)

The list sits under a visually hidden h2 'Notifications needing action', preceded by 'Show 1-8 of <total> results', or 'Show 0 of 0 results' when there are none; with more than eight notifications the page shows eight at a time, and following a page link keeps the sort and the category (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-actions.html:43-89, app/routes.js:6630-6688, 9050; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:160-161)

Each listed notification is shown with the same notification card as the live animals list, carrying its status tag, its error message and the links its status gives it (trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed action 15-16; document:dr1-parity-notes inc-030; conflicts:c-154)

The page's main content holds only its intro block, its search and sort form, its results line and its list; opening it with a delay-filter query parameter shows the same list as opening it without one (trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed snapshot 14; prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:9022-9023, 9043-9045)
The service navigation's 'Dashboard' item is marked current on the page (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8876, 9063; repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-076)

With the front door's stub mode on, which is never on in production, the page lists the built-in stub's notifications; otherwise it reads them from the notification read model, and the read model's log for that read carries the page request's trace id (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-062, p1-063)

If the read model cannot be loaded the page still shows its intro, shows the recoverable error message, responds with HTTP status 500 and logs the failure; with Welsh selected its copy shows in Welsh, marked as a machine draft; it has no serious or critical axe violations against the WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA tags (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-058, p1-079, p1-086)

The Status updated drill-down's Back link and current navigation item, for req-987 and req-967, are observed in that blocked row, and the Inspection required half of req-994 and req-1015 in that one.

Each is now an exhaustive positive check on what the page's main content holds.

rows.title: Search and sort the Action needed list
rows.detail: The Action needed page has a 'Search by' box and a 'Sort by:' select, and both are applied to the real list: the search matches a notification's number, commodity, consignee or consignor, and the sort is always applied, newest first when the page opens, with no unsorted state. The form is one GET form whose button submits the search and the sort together, so the page works with JavaScript turned off. The field and parameter names are the INS service's own. It waits with the page it searches.
acceptanceCriteria: The Action needed page has its own search form with a 'Search by' field and the hint 'Keyword, notification number, commodity, consignee or consignor'; a search made while the page is showing only live animals returns only live-animals notifications (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-actions.html:43-87; trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed snapshot 14, action 25; conflicts:c-250)

Searching for part of a listed notification's number, its commodity, its consignee's name or its consignor's name lists only the notifications that match; a search typed with surrounding spaces finds the same notifications, and a blank search lists them all (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-015; repo:tests repo-tests-p4-081; conflicts:c-155)
A search that matches nothing shows 'Show 0 of 0 results' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:7644-7658)

The 'Sort by:' select offers exactly 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', with 'Newest first' selected when the page opens; choosing one and pressing the form's button re-orders the list to match, and changing the select on its own submits nothing, so the page works with JavaScript turned off (trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed snapshot 14; document:dr1-parity-notes inc-031; conflicts:c-155, c-157)
Page links keep the chosen sort, the search text and the category (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-actions.html:43-87; trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed action 25)
With Welsh selected, the search label, the hint, the sort label and the sort options show in Welsh, marked as machine drafts (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-086)

Who: whoever owns the INS dashboard's requirements (the rulings do not name them) must firm them up and agree them with Sam.
notes: Kept apart from the Action needed page row so that row stays reviewable in one sitting, and because this one changes what the read model stores (consignee and consignor) and how it searches.
The same search form, sort select and results line are reused by the blocked Inspection required row, which proves its own half of req-990, req-992 and req-994.

The sort criterion now states the exact three options the select offers, which proves there is no fourth.

rows.title: Action needed glance card on the home's Live animals section
rows.detail: The home summarises each category with glance cards. The Live animals section gets its Action needed card, counted from the same set of notifications its page lists for the signed-in organisation, so the count is real rather than a fixed number. A notification's category is the one the animals backend stores on its record, an absent one meaning live animals. It waits until the notification dashboard's requirements are firmed up and agreed.
acceptanceCriteria: The Live animals section shows an 'Action needed' glance card reading 'Tasks requiring your attention', with a count and a 'View tasks' link that opens the Action needed page showing only live animals (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:57-62; trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 34; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:43; conflicts:c-250)

The Action needed count equals the number of results the Action needed page lists for live animals for the signed-in organisation: 0 for a fresh organisation, one higher once that organisation submits a live-animals notification without its ITAHC, and the same when another organisation does (conflicts:c-148, c-149)
A notification whose record carries no category is counted in the Live animals Action needed card (conflicts:c-296)

The Live animals section's only glance cards are 'Action needed' and 'Status updates' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:57-70; trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 30)
The Action needed card shows its count in the default count colour (trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 30; conflicts:c-156)

When the counts cannot be loaded the home still shows its heading and sections, shows the recoverable error message and responds with HTTP status 500; with Welsh selected the card's copy shows in Welsh, marked as a machine draft; the home still has no serious or critical axe violations (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-058, p1-079, p1-086)

Who: whoever owns the INS dashboard's requirements (the rulings do not name them) must firm them up and agree them with Sam.
notes: Combines every live-animals glance-card requirement that is not waiting on an outside feed: they share the home's template and the card styling. Depends on the home row for the sections and on the Action needed page row, because the count is that list's total.

req-975's germinal products half is observed in the Germinal products section row. req-978's blue Status updates and Inspection required counts are observed in the Status updated row and the plants-cards row, which build those cards.

The category comes from the animals backend's record (c-296); how it reaches the read model is the re-distil's to settle. The live-animals Status updates card (req-974) is held with its blocked drill-down (c-148).

Rewritten against the wording rules, keeping the row's id: the old title and detail named the design release, the old detail carried conflict ids, and one criterion stated the absence of an Inspection required card. That criterion now states the section's only two glance cards, which proves there is no third.

Changes the home's template and copy in the INS dashboard feature folder, which the split-off type-question-and-templates theme owns; it builds only after that theme lands, through the home row, so those files are in shared rather than touches.

rows.title: Status updates cards and the Status updated page
rows.detail: Each category gets a 'Status updates' card counting changes in the past 24 hours, opening a page that groups those notifications as Passed inspection, Needs inspection or Delayed. No service in the workspace receives inspection or delay outcomes and the INS read model holds no such state, so the cards and the page wait for the authorities' outcome feed rather than ship an always-empty page and a zero count. They also wait until the notification dashboard's requirements are firmed up and agreed.
acceptanceCriteria: The Live animals and Germinal products sections each show a 'Status updates' glance card reading 'Changes in the past 24 hours', its count in blue, with a 'View updates' link that opens the Status updated page showing only that category; each count equals the number of notifications that page lists for that category for the signed-in organisation (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:64-69, 73-98; trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 35; conflicts:c-148, c-156, c-250)

The 'View updates' link opens a page at /changes whose browser title is 'Changes in past 24 hours - Import notification service - GOV.UK', showing the caption 'Status updated', the h1 'Changes in past 24 hours' and the description 'Notifications that have progressed, or been validated, rejected, cancelled, or replaced in the past 24 hours.' together as one intro block styled to match the home's intro (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11712-11714, app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-changes.html:31-33; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:174-179)

The page groups the signed-in organisation's notifications of the category shown whose outcome changed in the past 24 hours under h2 sections 'Passed inspection', 'Needs inspection' and 'Delayed', in that order, showing a section only when at least one notification falls in it (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:6809-6825; trace:prototype-dr2-1 status-updated action 12-14, 21-22)

The page's main content holds only its intro block and its grouped lists; its 'Back' link goes to the notification list of the category it is showing, in that category's own frontend, and to the home while it is showing every category; the service navigation's 'Dashboard' item is marked current on it (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-changes.html:9-53; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:173-188; conflicts:c-295)

The page shows the recoverable error message with HTTP status 500 when the read model cannot be loaded, shows its copy in Welsh with Welsh selected, and has no serious or critical axe violations (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p1-058, p1-079, p1-086)

rows.title: Inspection required page
rows.detail: An 'Inspection required' page lists the signed-in organisation's consignments chosen for inspection at the border control post, across every category, with guidance on what to do at a border inspection. No service in the workspace receives which notifications are chosen for inspection, so the page waits for the authorities' feed rather than ship a list that is always empty. It also waits until the notification dashboard's requirements are firmed up and agreed.
acceptanceCriteria: The 'View requirements' link opens a page at /inspection whose browser title is 'Consignments due at the border control post (BCP) - Import notification service - GOV.UK', showing the caption 'Inspection required', the h1 'Consignments due at the border control post (BCP)' and the description 'Consignments that must go to your chosen BCP for inspection.' together as one intro block styled to match the home's intro (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11716-11718, app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-inspection.html:35-37; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:191-196)

rows.title: Germinal products section on the home
rows.detail: The home gets a Germinal products section, in a muted style, between Live animals and Plants, with its own View dashboard link to the germinal products list at the germinal products set root in the animals frontend, and its Action needed card. It waits until the notification dashboard's requirements are firmed up and agreed; its Status updates card waits with the Status updated page's count.
acceptanceCriteria: The home shows a 'Germinal products' section between 'Live animals' and 'Plants, plant products or other objects', in its muted style, with an h2 heading and a 'View dashboard' link that opens the germinal products notification list at the germinal products set root in the animals frontend (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:73-98; trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 33, 36; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:42, 45; conflicts:c-250, c-295, c-297)

The section shows an 'Action needed' card reading 'Tasks requiring your attention' with a count and a 'View tasks' link that opens the Action needed page showing only germinal products, and the section's only glance cards are 'Action needed' and 'Status updates' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8888-8894; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:45; conflicts:c-250)

The germinal products Action needed count equals the number of results the Action needed page lists for germinal products for the signed-in organisation, and a live-animals notification needing action is counted in the Live animals card (conflicts:c-148, c-149)

Following the germinal products 'View tasks', the Action needed page's 'Back' link goes to the germinal products notification list at the germinal products set root in the animals frontend (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-actions.html:12-24; conflicts:c-295)

rows.title: The plants section's glance cards
rows.detail: The home's plants section shows three glance cards, linking into the same three pages the live animals and germinal products cards do, once plants notifications reach the INS read model. The cards and their counts wait on the plants services publishing to that read model, on the authorities' feeds behind two of the pages they open, and until the notification dashboard's requirements are firmed up and agreed.
acceptanceCriteria: The plants section shows three glance cards: 'Action needed' with 'View tasks' opening the Action needed page showing only plants, 'Status updates' with 'View updates' opening the Status updated page showing only plants, and 'Inspection required' reading 'Consignments due at the BCP' with 'View requirements' opening the Inspection required page (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-home.html:100-131; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js:40, 46-48; conflicts:c-152, c-250)
Each plants card's count equals the number of notifications its page lists for plants for the signed-in organisation (conflicts:c-148, c-152)
The Status updates and Inspection required counts show in blue, and the Action needed count in the default count colour (trace:prototype-dr2-1 overall-dashboard action 30; conflicts:c-156)
openQuestions: Blocked: the plants services (trade-imports-plants-frontend and trade-imports-plants-backend) must publish their notifications to the INS read model in trade-imports-ins-backend before the plants glance cards can count or list anything. Who: whoever owns the plants services must add that publishing first.

Blocked: Sam's 9 October rulings also block these cards as INS dashboard summary information (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p3-062) until its requirements firm up and are agreed; the area is then re-distilled. Who: whoever owns the INS dashboard's requirements (the rulings do not name them) must firm them up and agree them with Sam.
notes: Depends on the Status updated and Inspection required rows as well as the live-animals card row, because two of its three links open those pages; both wait on the authorities' feeds, so this row needs them as well as the plants publishing.
trade-imports-plants-backend is not one of the programme's repos; its publishing is outside this row.
